utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session. Ms. Sutherland, you filed -- or you gave us this morning confidential Prosecution's reasons for requesting Rule 65 ter conference. First of all, I am lifting immediately the confidentiality because I see no reason why this should be treated confidential. It regards the management of the case and there should be nothing confidential about that. There should be absolute transparency.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. There is, in paragraph 10, if we could file a redacted version. It names the name of a witness who will be testifying in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That will be -- you will indicate that to the registrar. It will be redacted. But otherwise, the document itself will not be confidential. That's number one. Number two, I find objection to what you state in para 2, namely that on Monday, 10th June, 2003 a Rule 65 ter conference was held in chambers. You may think it was a Rule 65 ter conference. I think you ought to know that I invited, and together with the other two Judges, we invited you to a discussion in my chambers, never hinting at any given moment that this was going to be a formal 65 ter conference. So that is being corrected by the Chamber for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay. It's just a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I assumed that the meeting was pursuant to Rule 65 ter M, which says that the Trial Chamber can hold meetings in mutatis mutandis as they do pre-trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. It was not a 65 ter. It was -- was supposed to be a frank meeting between us. Mr. Cunningham --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, there's just one other paragraph I would like to correct, in paragraph 19. The word "not" was inadvertently missed out of the second sentence. It should read: "The brief was not an adequate response."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, Mr. Cunningham, I suppose -- I don't know whether this has already been notified to Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour. I got my copy this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But I suggest to you that you let Mr. Ackerman know about it, and we would like some kind of early response, because this is a matter that cannot be obviously left indefinitely to be discussed when he comes again, when he shows up again. So I would suggest to you to communicate this to him, and in particular, we would like -- first of all, we would like a response in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Secondly, in particular, he is asked to indicate whether he agrees with what is being described as being his position in paras -- or the Defence position in paras 28 and 29. And his comments or suggestions as regards what is stated or is being suggested by the Prosecution in para 30 of the document. If you can come back at the end of the break, or later on today, with some kind of response, that would be extremely helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will try to have that by the end of this break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. Also paragraph 11 needs to be redacted. That's -- a motion will be filed shortly for that evidence to be held in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And reference to it in paragraph 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: See with the -- indicate to the registrar which parts of this document you need -- or you require to be redacted and there will be no -- absolutely no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And there may be something in paragraph 12 that needs to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- no problem with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. No problems there. Yes. We'll reconvene at 11.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Before our last break --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Before the last break, the court asked me to contact Mr. Ackerman to discover -- to relay to the Court the Defence's response to the motion filed today by the OTP, specifically, paragraphs 28, 29, and 30. I've talked to Mr. Ackerman, and first of all we will have a written response to the Court tomorrow, but I can give the Court an idea of our position. Paragraph 28 deals with the time allocated for summation and closing arguments and the Prosecutor's request that it be reduced. With respect to paragraph 28 as per Mr. Ackerman, we have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take it that the Defence agrees that it will only require two days for its closing arguments.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fair, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Paragraph 29, Mr. Ackerman will let you know tomorrow, and I don't say that out of disrespect, that something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't expect something like this to be confirmed on two feet, without any prior notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And with respect to paragraph 30, the Prosecution clearly states that they're not aware of our view. I'll tell the Court and them, at this point we are not willing to reduce the time for filing our final briefs from four weeks to three weeks. We would like to keep it at four weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So we'll hear from you later on. And may I also ask you to confer with Mr. Ackerman, come back to us when you are in a position to do so. Last week, before Mr. Ackerman withdrew, or retired, he said that he was -- he would be thinking about the possibility of filing a motion asking for a longer period for more time to present -- to file the Rule 98 bis motion. Do you know anything with regard to that motion? We haven't received any motion it that effect, in any case, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I don't have anything to report to the Court on that, but I will guarantee the Court I'll have a report for you in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a break. We'll resume in 25 minutes from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 18th day of June 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.59 p.m.,
